translation: [It is] three cun, lying transversely above the Qiao and below the xi (cleft); look at where it is full and let blood. Wang Qixuan said: The vessel of Foot Taiyang follows the lumbar region, descends, and meets at the posterior yin, and so it is called Huiyin. The straight-yang vessel, flanking the spine and descending, pierces the buttocks to reach the popliteal fossa, follows the calf, crosses behind the outer ankle, and runs straight — and so it is called the straight-yang vessel.
